summary.headline: Godrej Properties Q4 FY26 bookings hit record INR10,163 crores (+21% QoQ); FY27 booking guidance set at over INR39,000 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record quarterly bookings of INR10,163 crores on 4,789 units and 7.3 mn sq ft, matching the prior best quarter and growing 21% QoQ. FY26 bookings reached INR34,171 crores (+16% YoY), 105% of guidance, and collections hit a record INR19,965 crores (+17% YoY). Q4 total income rose 47% to INR3,895 crores and net profit rose 70% to INR650 crores, with FY26 PAT at INR1,850 crores (+32%). Management guided FY27 bookings above INR39,000 crores and collections above INR24,000 crores, both about 20% growth, and reiterated a 20% ROE target by FY28. Management flagged the Middle East conflict and AI-related sentiment as near-term demand risks, while saying April footfalls and conversions held up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 residential bookings guided to over INR39,000 crores, about 20% above FY26 guidance and roughly 14% above FY26 actuals.
FY27 collections guided to over INR24,000 crores, about 20% growth; management noted FY26 collections missed the INR21,000 crore guidance by about 5%.
FY27 business development is not guided explicitly; management said FY27 FCF positive if BD is at guided levels (about INR20,000 crores GDV), with breakeven likely at levels similar to FY26.
Management expects FY28 to be strongly free cash flow positive, with a step-up in revenue recognition and collections as newer projects reach OC.
Target of 20% ROE by FY28 reiterated; annual 20% growth in guidance intended going forward.
Construction cost impact from the Middle East conflict estimated at 5% to 6% at most, with 0.1% to 0.2% quarterly margin impact to be recovered through price increases over 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: FY26 direct construction spend grew 62%; management said construction spend is running at about INR2,000 crores per quarter, with double-digit growth targeted in FY27.

Launch pipeline is large: NCR (Golf Links, Arden tower, Miraya phase), Mumbai (Bandra, Worli tower and phase, Kharghar and Panvel phases, Vikhroli in Q2 or Q3), Thane INR7,500 crore acquisition in late Q3 or Q4, and South, Pune, Kolkata, Raipur and Ahmedabad projects.
Acquired a large Gurgaon site whose approvals slipped; launch slated for Q1 FY27. Ashok Vihar (Delhi) is hoped for launch in FY27 but is not assured.
Around INR1,500 crores of milestone-linked land payments are pending for deals signed in FY26, payable in FY27.
Annuity portfolio is targeted at INR1,000 crores; GPL share is INR230 to 250 crores, with no near-term monetisation planned.
demand_pricing: Q4 sales were about 50% sustenance; FY26 mix was roughly 60% launches and 40% sustenance.

A pan-India sustenance campaign launched days before the call uses a 1% per month payment scheme with about 20% upfront and bullet payments. Management says it is a sourcing tool, not a PLP, and cap PLP-style discounts at 5% to 7% of quarterly sales.
Demand weakened in the last two weeks of March amid the Middle East conflict; management estimated about INR1,000 crores of sales were lost, and April footfalls and conversions have been reasonable.
Pricing is firm in South, Mumbai and Noida (supply shortage). Gurgaon price uptick is limited and management is not pushing price there.
FY26 volume growth was about 5%; management expects FY27 growth to be roughly equal in volume and value terms.
Inventory available for sale is 35% higher YoY on an opening basis.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 guidance achievable given NCR de-growth, AI concerns in Bengaluru and Pune, and geopolitical risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NCR's FY26 dip was due to slipped launches (Gurgaon approvals, Ashok Vihar) and expects NCR to return above INR10,000 crores. It sees AI worries as overdone and reasonable for guidance, and said the launch calendar is skewed to H1 and built bottom-up with buffers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of the Middle East war on demand, NRI inflows and construction costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand dipped in March but has since normalised somewhat; the Dubai-related shift to Indian property is expected to play out over time. Input costs are estimated to rise 5% to 6% at most, with a 0.1% to 0.2% quarterly margin impact, and forward contracts cover most inputs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep pursuing BD above its INR20,000 crore guidance, and when will FCF turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: BD depends on opportunities, and the balance sheet can support more than guided levels. At INR20,000 crores of BD, FCF should be positive; at FY26-like levels, breakeven. FY28 is expected to be strongly FCF positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did imputed EBIT margin fall to about 24.5% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a large Bengaluru 50-50 JV project (about INR4,000 crores of sales) and a fall in economic interest to 88% from 93%. PAT margin was at the top of the 10% to 15% guided range for a third year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the dividend being introduced, and what does it signal about cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said surplus cash will rise as BD investment normalises relative to cash generation, so dividends will be made consistent and growing. The FY27 dividend is modest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 collections and revenue recognition step up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the major revenue step-up in FY28 as OCs arrive, with about INR2,900 crores of revenue already linked to OCs. Economic interest has compounded at 55% a year over five years.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and possible prolonged supply shock affecting input costs (tiles and marble have seen constraints) and buyer sentiment; management says resolution in 2-3 months would allow a return to normal.
Launch timing slippage: Gurgaon, Ashok Vihar, Bandra and Worli launches depend on approvals, and FY26 collections already missed guidance by about 5%.
AI-related sentiment in Bengaluru and Pune, and softer Kharghar and Kharadi launches in late March.
Rising BD spend could delay FCF positivity in FY27; management said it is uncertain.
Sustenance campaign's 1% per month payment scheme could shift collection timing; watch pace of sales and collections in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 bookings and collection guidance and the launch calendar, but cautious on the Middle East conflict and buyer sentiment; answers on FY27 FCF and Ashok Vihar were hedged.
key_quotes: GPL delivered its best ever year for business development, bookings, collections, operating cash flow and earnings in financial year '26.
We remain extremely focused on delivering our return on equity target of 20% by financial year '28 by stepping up our speed on execution and project delivery.
So I think certainly, if we only add projects with INR20,000 crores, we'll certainly be free cash positive.
